svg.aria-label: The same memory array drawn three times at identical coordinates, with the highlight moving instead of the drawing. In the first panel every word line, bit line and cell is neutral grey, and a dashed orange rectangle is laid over one whole row and labelled as a page, which is how an abstract name gets pinned to a physical structure. In the second panel one word line and the cells along it turn green, and the caption says that selecting a row is a physical act performed on that one wire. In the third panel that green row stays and one bit line turns blue, with the single cell where they cross filled orange, which is the one cell being addressed. Closing notes state that the array is drawn once and only the highlight moves, because redrawing a dense figure for every step makes the reader find it again each time, that abstract names like page or row or block should be pinned onto the physical picture with a dashed box rather than only described in prose, and that two layers of highlight is the limit before a second figure is needed
svg.font-family: Poppins, 'Noto Sans SC', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
svg.text: DRAW THE ARRAY ONCE · MOVE THE HIGHLIGHT, NOT THE DRAWING
a dense figure redrawn for every step costs the reader a fresh search each time. keep it still, keep it neutral, and let one row or one cell come forward.
nothing selected
the structure, and nothing else
word
bit
one page
the dashed box is the whole point of this panel:
“page” is a word, and this is where it lives.
one word line up
selecting a row is a physical act
word
bit
the array did not move. one wire came forward,
and the cells it opens came with it.
one cell addressed
a row and a column, and their crossing
word
bit
two layers of highlight is the limit. a third
colour on the same picture and nothing is highlighted.
not part of this step
the word line that is up
the bit line being read
the one cell in question
a name, pinned to the structure
the array is drawn once. a dense picture redrawn for every step makes the reader locate it again in each panel, and by the third panel they have stopped looking carefully.
neutral is a choice, not a leftover. everything not part of this step is deliberately quiet, which is what gives the one thing that is coloured somewhere to stand out from.
a word like page, row, block or bank should be pinned onto the physical picture with a dashed box the first time it appears. described only in prose, it stays a word the reader nods at.
two layers of highlight is the working limit. a third colour on the same picture means nothing is highlighted, and it is the point at which the material wants a second figure.
Highlight in place · one array
